implementation_decisions: Driver: asyncpg 0.30.0 (mature SQLAlchemy-async integration); lazily imported so SQLite-only environments never need it

Serialization: write-first head upsert + SELECT ... FOR UPDATE re-read — SQLite keeps its writer-lock semantics, PostgreSQL holds the head row until commit; single-lock ordering avoids committer deadlocks
Retryable contention unified in app/kernel/dialects.py: SQLite lock/busy text + PostgreSQL SQLSTATEs 40001/40P01/55P03 feed the same bounded budget
Integrity mapping prefers the violated constraint name (asyncpg native) with the SQLite text match retained as fallback

Timestamps: all DateTime columns are timezone-aware (PostgreSQL TIMESTAMPTZ; SQLite rendering and contracts byte-identical) because the kernel stamps aware UTC and asyncpg rejects aware values against naive columns
PostgreSQL migration authority compares observed schema against the ORM contract directly; the migrations-vs-ORM reference diff stays on the SQLite profile (same chain and metadata feed both)
Legacy (pre-Alembic) database adoption is not offered on PostgreSQL — a PG database must be born from Alembic; documented fail-closed state
Migration-writer mutual exclusion on PostgreSQL is a pg_advisory_lock keyed by target database, released exactly when the holder connection closes

KernelPayloadStore is a minimal 3-operation protocol (stage/check_object/object_exists) — exactly what the commit path uses; larger store surface (read/delete/list) stays implementation-owned until PR83B needs it
known_deviations_between_profiles: PostgreSQL introspection is asynchronous: inspect_database(url) for PG URLs must run without a running event loop (CLI/worker thread); async callers use app.db_migration_postgres.inspect_database_async

Other kernel subsystems (events, fencing, gc, generations, liveness, publications, retention, scheduler) still use the SQLite-native upsert import and have not been exercised on PostgreSQL in this session
